text:
Sam (Support): FYI receiving a high-severity from ACME - their app is seeing lots of 504/502 gateway timeouts to the Redwood hosted API since 08:12 UTC. They say latency spikes then 5xx. I escalated.

Maya (Oncall): Acknowledged. Are errors coming from a single region or global? Any customer request ids?

Sam (Support): ACME provided request IDs and traces: 572c... mostly hitting iad-1. They reported a reproduction curl hitting /v1/generate that times out after ~15s.

Jon (eng-sre): Checking metrics now — seeing a correlation between increased request rate and pods not scaling fast enough. HPA shows no recent scale events until after the spike. Possibly KEDA scaler debounce or readiness causing slow pod warmup.

Elaine (prod-eng): Do we have recent deploys/rollouts around 08:00? deploy-bot, any rollouts?

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/model-serving-v2 -> canary -> 07:58 UTC. Canary passed health checks.

Maya (Oncall): Ok deploys overlap with the start. Need to collect pod events + readiness probe failures. Jon, can you paste the HPA and KEDA ScaledObject?

Jon (eng-sre): Here's what I pulled from the cluster (trimmed):
```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference model-api-hpa -o yaml
spec:
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 60
```
And KEDA ScaledObject snippet:
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1
kind: ScaledObject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: model-api-deployment
  pollingInterval: 30
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 50
  triggers:
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus.monitoring
        query: 'sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) / 1'
```
Jon (eng-sre): Note pollingInterval=30 and cooldownPeriod=300 — that's a big cooldown for bursty traffic. Also HPA target 60% CPU may not trigger quickly when container startup time is non-trivial.

Sam (Support): Customer says each new request during the burst hits a cold pod that spends ~8-12s loading model weights then times out at the gateway.

Elaine (prod-eng): That matches: model binary load time ~10s on cold start on that instance type. We depend on quick scale-up + warmup to avoid 504. Two issues: KEDA debounce too long + no prewarm startupProbe.

Alex (platform): I see readinessProbe is currently HTTP GET /healthz with failureThreshold: 3, periodSeconds: 10. Startup probe absent. So pod isn't marked ready until ~30s+ if startup is slow. HPA relies on readiness for endpoints and KEDA doesn't account for kernel-level warmup.

Maya (Oncall): Action items to mitigate immediate customer pain: 1) Increase minReplicaCount for ScaledObject to 3 in iad-1. 2) Add a lightweight startupProbe to mark container ready earlier (or separate warmup container). 3) Lower KEDA pollingInterval to 5s for this namespace and reduce cooldownPeriod to 60s. 4) Temporarily bump HPA minReplicas to 3 and reduce targetCPU to 40. Sam, can we ask ACME to retry traffic after ~2-3m?

Sam (Support): Confirmed with ACME — they're willing to hold traffic. Drafting a customer-facing note: "We've identified scale-up delays due to pod cold start and autoscaler debounce. We're applying changes and will monitor. Temporary mitigation: routing to warm pool; will update in 5-10 minutes."

Elaine (prod-eng): I'll open a PR to: 1) add startupProbe, 2) pre-pull model during init, 3) add lifecycle hook to download weights to tmpfs. PR link: https://git.redwood/model-serving/pulls/987 (will deploy to canary then region).

Jon (eng-sre): Running manual patch now to reduce KEDA polling in iad-1 and bump minReplicaCount:
```
kubectl -n inference patch scaledobject model-api --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":3,"pollingInterval":5,"cooldownPeriod":60}}'
kubectl -n inference scale deployment model-api-deployment --replicas=3
kubectl -n inference patch hpa model-api-hpa --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3,"metrics":[{"resource":{"name":"cpu","target":{"averageUtilization":40}}}]}}'
```
Jon (eng-sre): After scaling, backend pod count increased to 3 and request queue drained. Gateway 504s dropped.

CustomerBot: [automated] Alert cleared for ACME - 5xx error rate returned to baseline at 08:28 UTC.

Maya (Oncall): Can we add longer-term fixes: startupProbe + prewarm sidecar + keep-warm schedule or use warm pools reserved via Dedicated? Also add alerting for KEDA cooldown vs QPS growth.

Elaine (prod-eng): Agreed. Follow-ups: - Add startupProbe and pre-pull in PR - Add warm-pool job to keep N pods ready - Lower KEDA cooldown for bursty endpoints - Create runbook for similar escalations with repro steps and commands.

Jon (eng-sre): Repro steps I saved for the runbook:
1) Simulate burst: `hey -n 2000 -c 100 -q 5s http://<gateway>/v1/generate`
2) Observe pods: `kubectl get hpa -n inference model-api-hpa -w`
3) Check events: `kubectl get events -n inference --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp`
4) If cold-starts occur, test scaling: `kubectl scale deployment model-api-deployment --replicas=3`

Sam (Support): Customer update sent. They appreciated the quick mitigation. Marking incident as resolved but keeping follow-up tasks assigned. :thumbsup:

Maya (Oncall): Closing oncall incident. Follow-up tickets: PROD-542 (warm pools), PROD-543 (startupProbe + prefetch), PROD-544 (KEDA tuning).

Alex (platform): I'll also add a dashboard panel showing KEDA polling vs active QPS and an alert rule if qps increases > X while replicaIncreaseRate < Y.

Sam (Support): Thanks team. Logged notes and links in the Jira ticket.

Jon (eng-sre): Will keep monitoring for the next 2 hours and post any anomalies here.

Maya (Oncall): Good job everyone. :rocket:
